fieldValues.title: A wall reads as groups only where structure exists; where items share only words, grouping is a dream's job (five corpora measured)
fieldValues.summary: Readers round 2 (srs-lab#33), 2026-10-30. Each of 54 walls (sections of more than 15 items) in five corpora was grouped four ways: by kind, by a record the items link to, by tag, by a shared word. The default is the first of these that places 60% of the items with no group above 60%. Structure groups well where it exists: srs-context's 50 Findings by the component each applies to (the group label is a record a reader can open); the spec's Parts by kind; muSrs Evidence by tag (for, against, primary-text). All 10 LiveWyer walls and 9 of muSrs's 16 have nothing but words in common, and a word grouping is noise ('cannot', 'whether') even though it places 95% of items.
evidence: srs-lab readers/walls.js propose/best; the Reader page's Group by control
fieldValues.body: Two consequences. The share of items placed does not measure a grouping's quality: a word grouping scores highest and reads worst, so a cluster's quality needs a reader's test, not a coverage number. And the walls with no structure behind them are exactly where AI clustering (a dream that proposes and names groups) adds what neither the data nor a word count can; where structure exists, a client can group from it with no AI and no new data.
